Commentary.Commentary: That's a wrap to the fourth T20I. Australia have avoided the ignominy of a whitewash with this victory and would be now aiming to make it 3-2 before flying home. Bangladesh though would want to hold the trophy after winning for one final time in the series. Who will come out on top? Do join us on Monday, 9th August 2021 to find out. The first ball will be at 6 pm local (12 pm GMT) but you can join us in advance for the build-up. Cheers!

Matthew Wade, the Aussie skipper, smiles and says that they have worked hard in the last few games and it was nice to get the result. Calls the knock of Dan Christian as the difference between winning and losing. Shares that the move to send him at number 3 was planned this morning as they needed to find some runs at the top as finding the runs at the backend was proving to be tough. Mentions that Christian is a terrific hitter and thankfully he did the job. States that it would have been nice to get some runs from a few players including him. Feels that they are not batting poorly but the conditions are tough and they are trying to find a way. Hopes to put runs on the board in the next match. Tells that the bowlers have dominated the series and you are looking for a quick 30s or 40s from a batter to win the match. He hints that they might play three spinners in the next game.

THE PLAYER OF THE MATCH IS MITCHELL SWEPSON! The leggie says that it was nice to get the nod to play and the conditions were nice to bowl. Shares that he has not experienced these conditions back home. Tells that on a wicket like this he found it hard to let the ball go straight and he was trying to be accurate and hit the stumps. On his mindset when he was on a hat-trick, Swepson replies that he forgot he was on a hat-trick but in hindsight, it was a good ball but the batsman got a bat on it.

Mahmudullah, the captain of Bangladesh, says that it was always difficult to chase and feels they didn't assess the wicket well as it was 120-130 surface and they were a few runs short. Praises the bowlers for stretching the match to the 19th over and as a batting unit, Mahmudullah feels that they need to be cautious and sensible. Mentions that the surface used in this match was the hardest so far and wants to look forward and maximize their opportunity in the batting order. Admits that Dan Christian's batting changed the whole scenario but they know Shakib Al Hasan is a champion bowler and he will come back stronger. On holding back Mustafizur Rahman, the Bangla captain replies that he had to keep his two overs as they were defending a low total. Signs off by saying that the bowlers did their job but the batters didn't put their hands up.
Time for the presentation...

Earlier in the day, Mitchell Swepson led Australia's charge with the ball and played an important role in restricting Bangladesh to a paltry total. Ashton Agar and Ashton Turner played their part with the ball as well, while Josh Hazlewood continued to impress with his accuracy. It was the bowling effort that didn't allow Bangladesh to score more than 104, otherwise, you know what would have happened.

In a run chase of 105, Australia found themselves in a good position when Dan Christian expressed himself with the bat. They were cruising inside the Powerplay but after his departure, once again it was a steady procession for the Aussies. From 47/1 to 65/6, the touring team pushed themselves into a hole and had the Ashtons not combined for a valuable 34-run alliance, it would have been yet another embarrassing loss for the Kangaroos on this tour.

The Bangla bowlers once again were very impressive. Mahedi Hasan and Nasum Ahmed's 8 overs combined squeezed the life out of the Australian chase and had Shakib Al Hasan not gone for 50 runs in his 4 overs, the picture could have been different. A word of praise for Mustafizur Rahman, he was exceptional yet again and in hindsight, Mahmudullah brought him too late when the stand between Ashton Turner and Ashton Agar was prospering. Still, you have to say, well-tried Bangladesh, although a golden chance of inflicting a whitewash has slipped away.

A hard-earned win for Australia. They have huffed and puffed to reach the target of 105 runs. It tells you that their batting woes have not ended yet. The tourists decided to throw caution to the wind in the run chase as they sent Dan Christian up the order at number 3. The Aussie all-rounder emerged with positive intent and hammered 5 sixes in one over bowled by Shakib. His knock turned out to be vital as the Aussies lost the plot after that but the required rate never bothered them.

AUSTRALIA WIN BY 3 WICKETS! A length delivery on middle and off, Tye offers a straight bat defense and keeps it out on the off side. Turner spots the chance and calls his partner through for a quick run. All over, Australia have finally crossed the line!
Very full and outside off, Tye is way too early into the shot and misses.
Swing and a miss! Tye wants to finish with a flourish but connects only with thin air. Angling away, on a length, Andrew aims for a shot down the ground but misses.

A touch short in length and angling down the leg side, Tye swings his bat firmly across the line and gets a top edge. It falls in no man's land away from the fine leg fielder and the batsmen take two. Scores are levelled.

Mix-up! Angling away from the batsman, Tye pushes it down to backward point and Turner shows interest in a run. Tye comes out of the crease but then is sent back as the fielder misses his shy at the striker's end.
Too full in length and around off, Turner squeezes it out past the diving point fielder for a run.
Slower one, full and outside off, Turner forces it down the ground and the mid off fielder circles around it. A single to complete the over. 4 needed more.
Short in length and outside off, Tye pulls and the mid on fielder dives across to his right to stop the racing ball. Saves three.
Good length ball on middle, Tye turns it to mid-wicket.
Andrew Tye is the new batsman. 6 needed more.

OUT! Shamim Hossain has taken a stunner! It's not over yet! Shoriful angles in a full length ball on middle, Agar finds it in his range and aims to go down the ground. He though fails to keep it down and Shamim dives full length to his right at mid on to take a stunning catch. Perfectly timed dive.
Commentary.Howout: c Shamim Hossain b Shoriful Islam

Commentary.Commentary: Slightly short and outside off, slower in pace, Agar cuts but finds the point fielder. He is not happy with himself.
FOUR! Under 10 needed now. Back of a length delivery outside off, Agar camps back and smacks it through extra cover for a boundary.
Who will bowl from this end now? Shoriful Islam is running in.
Angling away from the batsman, outside off, Turner stands back with an open stance to cover his stumps and then allows it through.
On a length and outside off, Agar goes deep inside the crease and then guides it to the right of short third man for a run. 10 needed more.
And again. From a length outside off, Mustafizur Rahman gets it to curl back into the batsman, Agar is cramped for room again and somehow defends it out.

The Fizz bowls a cutter which deviates towards the batsman with extra bounce. Agar tries to cut but is cramped for room. It takes his gloves and rolls on the leg side. Turner wants a run but is sent back.
Beaten all ends up! A fuller length ball outside off, cutting back in, Agar aims for a booming drive but it beats the inside edge.
A low dipping full toss on off, Agar closes the face of his bat and helps it gently through mid-wicket. It's placed well and they collect a couple of runs.
Mustafizur Rahman is back into the attack. 2-1-2-2 are his figures so far.
Full and flighted on off, it's driven down to long off for a run. 7 runs from the over, 13 needed off 24 balls.
Shakib brings his length back and delivers it on off, Turner moves back and taps it down to point for one.
Fires a full ball on middle, Turner defends it away off the inner edge to mid-wicket.
Loopy and full on off, Turner lunges and defends it back.
Flatter and on middle, tucked through square leg for a run.
FOUR! A much-needed boundary for Australia to bring the equation further down. Fuller in length and on off, it's drilled down the ground and beats the diving attempt of long on.
Shakib Al Hasan is back on. 20 needed off 30 balls.
Oooohhh...this one almost went through! Mahmudullah has his hands on his head. That was very full. Loopy off spinner on off, Turner strides forward to drive but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
A slider from the Bangla skipper, on the shorter side, Agar goes back and slaps it to deep cover for a single.
Quicker one, full and outside off, pushed with an angled bat to point.
Short this time, around off, Turner punches it down to long off for one.
Tossed up ball around off, Turner pushes it to the right of the extra cover fielder and Mahedi dives to parry it towards the bowler.
Flights it and lands it full outside off, Agar drives it to deep cover for a single.
Mahmudullah to bowl himself.
Short and wide outside off, Turner rocks back to pull but ends up dragging it off the inside edge to square leg. A dot ball to finish Nasum Ahmed's spell too, 4-0-17-1 are his figures.
Loopy and full on middle, Turner defends it back with a straight blade.
Quicker one, short and around leg, Agar goes back and works it behind square leg for one. 23 needed more.
Full and on off, pushed back to the bowler.
Wide! Fires one down the leg side, Agar fails to work around.

SIX! Agar takes a calculative risk and it pays off. Tossed up ball landing full on middle, Agar goes down on one knee and slog sweeps it with the spin. Not timed it well but enough to clear the fielder in the deep.

Edged but just beyond first slip! Loopy delivery, full and around off, it spins away with extra bounce, Turner tries to defend but it takes the shoulder of the bat and loops in the air. It's wide of Sarkar. The batsmen cross.

Fullish and on off, Turner drives it to the left of long off and runs the first run hard. The fielder though attacks the ball and the Aussie pair decide not to risk the second run. 32 needed off 42 balls. 4-0-17-2, Mahedi Hasan has bowled out. Outstanding.
Presses forward to a full ball and drives it to covers where Soumya Sarkar dives across to his left and stops the ball.
Loopy off spinner on off, landing full, Turner is forward as he defends it from the inside portion of his bat.
Fires in a fuller length ball on off, Agar drives it down to long off for a single.
Short and around off, Agar steps back to make room and whacks it to deep cover for a couple of runs.
Slider, around middle and leg, Agar defends it close to his pads and gets an inside edge.
Short in length and wide outside off, Agar goes back and slaps it to deep cover-point for a single. 36 runs needed off 8 overs.

Pitches it up and around off, Turner pushes it gently towards cover-point. They rush across for a run as Shamim Hossain picks up the ball. He loses his balance though and is unable to release the throw.
Back of a length ball on middle, not allowing the batsman any width to work with, Turner tucks it to mid-wicket.
Accurate bowling, on a length around middle, Turner defends it down on the leg side.
Angling down the leg side, Agar tries to flick but fails to connect cleanly. It goes off his pads and rests beside the pitch. The batters steal a leg bye.
Starts his spell with a good length ball on off, Agar defends it from the back foot to the off side.
Shoriful Islam to bowl for the first time in this innings.
Too full in length and on middle, Agar drills his drive to deep cover for a single.
Floated one, full and on off, Agar lunges and blocks it down.
Short and wide outside off, cut off the back foot to point.
Fullish and on middle, defended back to the bowler.
Ashton Agar is in next.

OUT! BOWLED 'EM! Big blow to Australia, the man in form for Australia has a rare flop show. A flatter full delivery, around off and turning in, Marsh decides to drive it through the line but misses and finds his stumps shattered. Mitch has a smile on his face as he returns. Got outfoxed there by Mahedi. 40 needed off 58 balls.
Full and flighted around off, Turner goes down and across to sweep and gets it away off the inner half. The ball races away to fine leg for a single.
Fuller in length and around middle, Marsh defends it back. At the halfway mark, Australia need 41 more for a win.

Huge shout for a caught behind! The Fizz delivers it very full and wide outside off, Marsh tries his best to drive but misses. There is some sound but it appears to be from the bat hitting the deck. Bangladesh have opted against the DRS. The replays, later on, show that there was a spike!
A touch short in length and around leg, Turner moves across a bit and glances it down to fine leg for a run.
Ashton Turner is the new batsman.
Alex Carey has been given out lbw. He takes the referral. Is the impact outside off? Doesn't look like it.

OUT! Carey is a dead duck! He has to depart! Clever change in pace from The Fizz. He dishes out his cutter again and lands it full around off, Carey is late in getting forward to defend and is thudded on the pads. They appeal and the umpire agrees. Carey takes a hesitant referral but it's of no use. Three reds on the Ball Tracker and Australia have now lost 5 wickets. 42 needed off 63 balls.
Wrong line, on a good length outside leg, Marsh tucks it behind square leg and picks up a single.
A cutter, landing around leg, Marsh plays close to his body and pushes it out safely to the off side.
Bowling change. Mustafizur Rahman is back on.
Arm ball, landing full on off, Marsh tries to drive but gets an inside edge. It rolls on the leg side and they cross. 2 from the over, 43 needed off 66 balls.
Identical to the last delivery, Alex hangs back and forces it to sweeper cover for one.
Flatter one, short and on off, Carey goes on the back foot and pushes it to covers.
Nearly another wicket! A quicker one, full and on off, spinning away, Carey pushes it early and chips it back in the direction of the bowler. It falls short of Mahedi as he reacts forward.
Slower one, full and on off, Alex lunges and defends it on the leg side.
Quicker and fuller on off, skidding in, Carey defends it off the inner half to mid-wicket.
Alex Carey is the new batsman. 45 needed off 72 balls. Also, Mahedi Hasan is back on.

OUT! RUN OUT! Unfortunate way to get out and Henriques has to go! Flatter ball on middle, Marsh punches it straight back to the bowler. Shakib seems to have got his hand on it before it hits the stumps at his end. He appeals and the third umpire is called. The replays show that Henriques is definitely short and Shakib Al Hasan has got a fingertip on it.

Appeal for a run out at the bowler's end. Has the bowler got some fingertips on the ball? Is Moises Henriques backing up too much? The touch from the bowler seems to be there but the third umpire needs to be convinced. Moises is short for sure and the third umpire feels that Shakib has deflected it. Australia lose their 4th wicket.
On off, pushed to cover.

FOUR! What a hit that is! Tossed up on off, Marsh gets back and then lifts it over extra cover. The umpires check if it is a six or a four and the replays show that it has hit the ropes on one bounce.
Four or Six? The third umpire is referred and it's found out that the ball bounced just in front of the rope.
Flatter ball on off, Henriques punches it down to long off for a single.
Full on off, Moises pushes it to extra cover where the fielder makes a half stop. Two taken.
A slip in place now along with a leg gully.
Flatter ball on off, Marsh punches it to deep cover for one.
Shakib Al Hasan is back on. He was taken to the cleaners in his last over, by Dan Christian, who hammered him for 5 sixes in an over.
Loopy ball on middle, Henriques pushes it back to the bowler.
Full on off, Marsh drives it to long off for a single.
Flatter ball outside off, Marsh cuts it to point.
Tossed up on off, Henriques pushes it down to long off for a single.
Full on middle, Henriques works it to mid on.
The physio comes out. Nurul Hasan has taken a blow on his helmet while collecting the throw. A mandatory concussion test is conducted and the wicketkeeper is fine.

Flighted ball on middle, Marsh sweeps it to short fine leg for a single. The fielder fires in a flat throw to the keeper who jumps to collect it. It seems to have gone through his gloves and pinged him on the helmet. Yes, that's the case.
Full on middle, Henriques defends it out. Australia are 49 for 3 at the end of the Powerplay. They need 56 more in 84 balls.
Slight halt in play. There is an issue with the landing area of the bowler. Som sawdust is being applied and Mustafizur Rahman is good to continue...
Another slower one outside off, Henriques gets deceived as he looks to defend but misses.
Back of a length ball on off, Henriques goes on his back foot and then defends it to point.
BEATEN! Good length ball around off, Henriques looks to defend but misses.
Moises Henriques is the new batsman.

OUT! CAUGHT! Christian goes after playing a fine little cameo and Bangladesh are clawing back in the game now. Slower ball outside off, at 106 kph, Christian looks to go over point but it goes off the upper half to Shamim Hossain at point who makes no mistake.
Commentary.Howout: c Shamim Hossain b Mustafizur Rahman

Commentary.Commentary: Slower ball around off, Christian looks to pull but is way early into the shot and he misses.
Mustafizur Rahman is into the attack.

Edged but there is no slip in place. Tossed up ball landing full around off, Marsh tries to defend but it spins away to take the outside edge. The ball hurries wide of the keeper and rolls away from short third man. The batsmen take two. 4 runs and a wicket from the over, 56 needed off 90 balls.
Shout for an lbw, not given. Fuller and on off, Marsh looks to defend but gets an inside edge onto the pads. The umpire turns down the appeal.
Mitchell Marsh comes out now.

OUT! Trapped in front! Nasum has a wicket against the run of play. The last ball turned a lot and this time Ahmed delivers it flat and on middle. This time it straightens just a touch after landing, Ben McDermott is caught on the back foot as he fails to work it away. He is pinged on the pads, they appeal and the finger has gone up. Ben nods looking at his partner and walks away.
Turn and bounce outside off, Ben tries to defend but misses.
Too full in length on off, forced down to long off for one.
Loopy and full on middle, worked on the leg side for a run at mid-wicket.

SIX! Make it five maximums in the over! Unbelievable hitting. This is why he has been sent at number 3. Shakib drops it short and on middle, Dan Christian goes on the back foot and rockets his pull shot over mid-wicket. 30 from the over, 60 needed more.
SIX! Dan Christian is on a roll here. Brutal. Full and flighted, right in the slot around off, Dan gives it the full whack of his bat and dispatches it over long on.
Swing and a miss! Shakib bowls it slower and lands it full and outside off, Christian tries to slog sweep but it spins past his bat.
SIX! Hat-trick of biggies! Dan Christian is motoring. Loopy and full on middle, Christian again goes down on one knee and plunders it over mid-wicket. 18 from the first three balls.
SIX! And again! Shakib tosses this one around off, lands it full and outside off, Christian kneels and smokes it over long on.

SIX! This one has gone the distance! Christian does pack a punch. He has come out with the license to attack and does that by charging down the track. He reaches the fuller length in a flash and dismisses it over wide long on.
Quicker and on off, Ben McDermott goes on the back foot and punches it to short extra cover. Fantastic over, only one from it.
Flatter one, it's fired full on off, McDermott defends it back with a straight blade.
Short again, around off and turning away, Ben goes back and punches it to covers.
Flatter and shorter on middle, DC moves back and is hurried into the pull shot. Works it wide of mid on and crosses for a run.
Beaten again! Tossed up ball around off, turning away with extra bounce, Christian tries to slog sweep but it bounces over his bat.
Nasum Ahmed is on now.
Beaten! Flatter and shorter around off, too close to cut but Dan still tries and gets beaten.
Full and floated on off, Ben McDermott leans and defends it back watchfully. 5 from the over, 91 needed off 108 balls.
Nicely tossed up, full and outside off, McDermott allows it to spin away and pushes it with an angled bat to point.
Wide! Shakib fires a short delivery down the leg side, Ben tries to buy some cheap runs but misses.
Tossed up ball pitching outside off, McDermott takes a long stride forward and drives it through extra cover for a couple.
Loopy ball, landing full around off and skidding in, Ben presents a straight bat in defense but it takes the inner edge and rolls to short mid-wicket.
Full and flighted on off, Christian goes down on one knee and swipes it through mid-wicket for a single.
Slower through the air, full and around leg, McDermott works it in front of square leg for one.
Shakib Al Hasan will bowl from the other end.

FOUR! Up and over! Dan is sent up the order to score some quick runs. Flatter and fuller outside off, Christian latches onto it and pumps it over mid off for a boundary. 9 from the over, under 100 needed for Australia.
Straightaway Christian shows intent. Flighted delivery, full and outside off, Dan lofts it over extra cover and opens his account with a couple of runs.
Dan Christian is the next man in.

OUT! SOUND OF TIMBER! Mahedi hurls in a slider around off, at 95 clicks, it lands around off and zips off the surface. Wade is on the front foot, looking to defend but his bat is way away from the line of the delivery. A big gap between bat and pad and it's a safe passage for the ball to sneak through and destroy the stumps behind. Another dismal outing for Wade!
Quicker this time, full and on off, Wade defends it by getting foward.
Loopy one, full and outside off, Wade lunges to defend but gets a genuine edge wide of first slip. It runs down to third man and they take a couple.
Tossed up ball, landing on middle and spinning down, McDermott goes back and works it through mid-wicket for a single.
